title: A deterministic polynomial chaos Galerkin method for non-Markovian quantum state diffusion
abstract: Developing general-purpose numerical methods for non-Markovian quantum state diffusion has long been a challenge in the simulation of open quantum systems. This paper proposes a deterministic polynomial chaos Galerkin method, which is easy to implement, accurate, and efficient. By combining a low-rank decomposition of bath correlations with Galerkin projection onto a polynomial chaos basis, the method yields a deterministic formulation compatible with standard numerical solvers for partial differential equations. The reduced density matrix is obtained from a single deterministic solve at a cost comparable to that of computing one stochastic hierarchy trajectory. Replacing an ensemble of $N_{\mathrm{traj}}$ trajectories therefore reduces the computational cost by approximately a factor of $N_{\mathrm{traj}}$ and eliminates statistical sampling error. Benchmark comparisons show that the proposed method achieves smaller errors at lower computational cost than the tested stochastic hierarchy methods. Applications involving nonquadratic potentials, diffraction and interference, and coupled three-dimensional dynamics demonstrate its ability to handle challenging problems.
summary: This paper introduces a deterministic polynomial chaos Galerkin method (DPCG) to solve the challenging non-Markovian quantum state diffusion problem. By replacing ensemble averaging with a single deterministic solve based on low-rank decomposition and polynomial expansion, the method drastically cuts computational costs. It proves to be highly accurate and efficient for simulating open quantum systems like the spin-boson model.
main_problem: Developing general-purpose and computationally efficient numerical methods for simulating non-Markovian quantum state diffusion (NMQSD) in open quantum systems.
main_result: The proposed deterministic polynomial chaos Galerkin method (DPCG) achieves accuracy comparable to stochastic hierarchy methods while drastically reducing computational cost by eliminating the need for large ensembles of trajectories.
method: The method combines a low-rank decomposition of bath correlations with a Galerkin projection onto a polynomial chaos basis, transforming the stochastic evolution into a single, deterministic set of partial differential equations for the expansion coefficients.
model_or_system: The study focuses on open quantum systems whose dynamics are governed by the NMQSD equation, exemplified by the spin-boson model and the Caldeira-Leggett model. The system interacts with an environment modeled by bath correlations.
key_observables: The reduced density matrix ($ho(t)$), spin polarization ($\langle\sigma_zangle_t$), and the state error ($\|\psi_t - \psi_{Q,P,t}\|_X$).
important_parameters: Low-rank truncation order ($Q$), polynomial chaos total degree ($P$), and the coupling strength ($\xi$ or $\varepsilon$).
main_assumptions: The primary approximations involve truncating the infinite-dimensional bath correlation function via low-rank decomposition and truncating the polynomial chaos expansion at a finite total degree $P$.
figures_summary: Benchmark comparisons (e.g., for the spin-boson model) show the DPCG method maintaining accuracy comparable to reference solutions at strong coupling, while computational cost is significantly lower than stochastic methods.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the challenge of NMQSD and compares it to existing stochastic methods (HOPS/LRS). It then details the DPCG formulation, deriving the deterministic coefficient system via low-rank factorization and Galerkin projection. Finally, it presents convergence analysis and benchmarks on physical models.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, deterministic alternative to computationally expensive stochastic methods for simulating open quantum dynamics, making complex, memory-dependent quantum processes accessible for routine simulation.
